title: Add TransportSelector which helps users to select the optimal transpo…

timeline.message:
Add TransportSelector which helps users to select the optimal transport implementation for their platform

Motivation:

At the moment most users manually check if netty provides a native implementation for their platform and if so select it. This pattern is present in almost all code bases by end-users. We should provide this functionality out of the box so users dont need to maintain it by themselves.

Modifications:

Add TransportSelector which will pick the right Channel / EventLoopGroup implementation based on the platform and what native libs are on the classpath

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/10076
timeline.author: Norman Maurer

This is very similar that we have in our code :). But sometimes we need to change transport from native to NIO and vice versa. What about create  interface `TransportFactory` with methods `socketChannel`, `datagramChannel`, ... etc and create enum or class `TransportFactorySelector` where defined implementations `NIO`, `EPOLL`, `KQUEUE` and additional method `platformDepend` that will return transport according current OS or we can chose transport manually (e.g. TransportFactorySelector.NIO)

reply.body:
this is a bit of a nit (in response to the above):
Why not just create a small class to hold all of them.

```java
TransportSelections selections = TransportSelector.selectOptionalForNative();
```

Something like `TransportSelections`, `TransportStrategy`, `TransportSettings`, `TransportConfiguration`, etc. might make sense. It might also lend itself to being more DI-friendly.

However, rather than `Tuple#configureBootstrap(Bootstrap)`, I think the opposite direction would be more user-friendly, something like `Bootstrap#configure(Tuple)`.

I think tuple is a bit of an anti-pattern on the GC side of things and it's not commonly used by netty, unless it's some kind of `static final` variables.
But since it's only used one time during app bootstrap it doesn't matter much...

timeline.body:
👍 
so much code on GitHub does this with varying logic to turn on/off native NIO.
Not sure why you'd even want to turn off native NIO if it's available on the classpath.

In such a case those few edge cases than fallback to their custom implementation.


Would it make sense to add **os-selector** maven plugin to transport-selector?
**transport-selector** should have the correct native-transport as a dependency!
(as a runtime dependency)

As I mentioned in the other issue, there are some use cases where users or applications may prefer to fail outright, rather than silently defaulting to a non-native transport. E.g., perhaps you expect Epoll to be available, and silently defaulting to Nio might have dangerous performance implications.

I'm okay with saying that is too niche of a use case for us to be concerned with here, but I'm also wondering if we should we consider offering some way to *require* a native transport? Perhaps an accompanying `NativeTransportSelector`? Or `require` variations of the methods?

I like the direction of the class, but I'm worried that it doesn't do much to address the major problem for many users: discoverability. I would like to see a way for this class to be automatically integrated into `Bootstrap` and `ServerBootstrap`.

Following this change, I think we should consider deprecating the constructors for those classes, and replace them with static constructors (or builders) that resemble something like: `Bootstrap.forTcpServer()` that will automatically call methods like `TransportSelector.serverSocketChannel()`.

@Bennett-Lynch the problem is that we can't really put it in transport as it would have been some cycle dependencies :/ Sure we could hack around this by using reflection etc but this just sounds wrong. That is also why I did add it to a new jar so we dont have the issue.

> This is very similar that we have in our code :). But sometimes we need to change transport from native to NIO and vice versa. What about create  interface `TransportFactory` with methods `socketChannel`, `datagramChannel`, ... etc and create enum or class `TransportFactorySelector` where defined implementations `NIO`, `EPOLL`, `KQUEUE` and additional method `platformDepend` that will return transport according current OS or we can chose transport manually (e.g. TransportFactorySelector.NIO)

There is already existing flag `io.netty.transport.noNative` that helps to quickly switch from native transport to NIO. Because it's not practical to switch between `epoll <-> kqueue` and the only ways are `epoll -> nio` / `kqueue -> nio` I think that flag is enough instead of doing a code change.

Because it's not practical to switch between `epoll <-> kqueue` and the only ways are `epoll -> nio` / `kqueue -> nio` I think that flag is enough instead of doing a code change.

@idelpivnitskiy Thx, I missed this flag. What if we disabled native transport via `system.properties` and now `Epoll.isAvailable() -> false` and for first `Bootstrap` client we use `NIO` but for second I want to use `Epoll` currently according `TransportSelector` I cannot do this (because `Epoll.UNAVAILABILITY_CAUSE` is static final).
Right, if the `io.netty.transport.noNative` flag is used, it affects the whole JVM. How practical is it to have mixed transports in one app?

> Right, if the `io.netty.transport.noNative` flag is used, it affects the whole JVM. How practical is it to have mixed transports in one app?

You right, In practice in most cases we will have one transport (`NIO`, `EPOLL`,  `KQUEUE`) on production except (e.g. A/B testing) or something else. Also in our tests suite we have different scenarios and benchmark to check correct app behavior to each transport and for us it would be convenient to have this ability.

I think the classifiers should be probably be included here? i.e.
```
<classifier>linux-x86_64</classifier>
```
